catalog_quote: 4. Stress. In all four languages stress is contrastive and thus phonemic. Examples of contrastive stress are as follows: Maiani /'ɑpɑ/ 'father's sister' /ɑ'pɑ/ 'season' /'uṯum/ 'wet' /u'ṯum/ 'hide' /'uşişi/ 'he shot it and' /u'şişi/ 'he gave it to him and' /'ṉeşike/ 'he is giving it to you (pl)' /ṉe'şike/ 'he is giving it to you (sg)' ... An interesting feature of stress has been noted in comparing two syllable words that are similar in all four languages. Maia tends to stress the first syllable, whereas Maiani, Miani and Mala stress the second syllable. /'ɑrop/ 'three' (Maia) /ɑ'řop/ 'three' (Maiani, Miani) /ŋgɑ'řop/ 'three' (Mala) /'ulum/ 'dirty' (Maia) /u'lum/ 'dirty' (Maiani, Mala) /u'řum/ 'dirty' (Miani)

Maia tends…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Maiani is contrastive (phonemic): its position is not predictable and distinguishes lexical items and even inflected verb forms (e.g. 2pl vs 2sg object forms 'nesike / ne'sike). The only positional generalisation offered is a tendency: in disyllabic words cognate across the family, Maiani (with Miani and Mala) stresses the second syllable where Maia stresses the first. Stress is not marked in the orthography. The SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (May 1994) repeats 'Stress is phonemic' with the same minimal pairs.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source.
new_statements.exceptions: No rule, hence no exceptions; authors note only 'a couple of words which are ambiguous because of stress' when stress is left unwritten (sec. 5.3, pp. 13-14), and that /r/ is realised as a flap between vowels in unstressed syllables (2.4.2, p. 6).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on isolated (citation) forms, including inflected verbs; minimal pairs given in phonemic slashes with a stress mark before the stressed syllable. No discussion of phrase-level prominence or acoustic correlates. The paper covers four Kaukombaran languages; the Maiani data are first-hand (authors resident in a Maiani village, footnote p. 1).
new_statements.identity_note: Both primary sources describe Maiani [tnh] proper (May & Loeweke worked from a Maiani-speaking village; the OPD is headed 'Maiani (Tani, Miani South) [TNH]', villages Simbine, Tamokot, Ulatapun, Erevenam). The 1985 paper treats four Kaukombaran languages together; the quoted phonemic-stress statement is made for all four, with separate Maiani minimal pairs, and the second-syllable tendency is stated jointly for Maiani, Miani [pla, Glottolog mian1254] and Mala [ped], contrasting with Maia [sks]. Z'graggen's 'Tani' covers both Miani and Maiani; Pick 2020 notes Z'graggen's published Tani wordlist is Miani, not Maiani. Wikipedia merges Maiani into 'Miani language'.
